title: The direction budget this run was given is not the direction budget it used
detects: An artefact whose direction ceiling and applied direction count disagree. `max_directions` is what the search was allowed to use and `num_directions` is what the saved model actually had removed, and the search picks its budget inside the ceiling, so the two come apart routinely. It says which of the two numbers a reader should quote. It does not say the run went wrong, because on a single artefact it did not.
incident: Ours, 2026-08-03, at one remove. A five-seed comparison of a one-direction arm against a three-direction arm finished at p equals 0.004 and was withdrawn in full, because both arms had ablated one direction per layer: the arms were named after their ceilings and the ceilings were not what ran. Nothing in either artefact was false. The ceiling and the applied count were both recorded, and the comparison was built on the first, which is why the number a reader quotes from a single file is worth naming even when nothing is wrong with the file.
remedy: Quote `num_directions` with `dir_mode`, which is what was applied, and treat `max_directions` as what it is: a ceiling on the search. If two arms were meant to differ in direction budget, compare them with `--pair`, which runs the check that can see whether their applied counts actually differ.
false_positive: A ceiling above the applied count is the NORMAL outcome of a search that was free to use fewer directions, so this fires on most honest runs with `--max-directions` above one and is not reporting a defect when it does. That is why it is `notes` and not a withdrawal: the finding is that two numbers in this artefact could be read for each other, and the reader is entitled to know which is the edit. It cannot see whether anybody actually quoted the ceiling, which is the thing that would turn it into an error, and it cannot see the case it comes from at all, which is two arms that agree when they were supposed to differ. That case needs two artefacts and belongs to `an-arm-labelled-by-a-setting-it-did-not-apply`.
